name: Margaux

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
A ranking for Médoc châteaux left out of the 1855 classification. Any Médoc property may apply.

In 1855 brokers ranked Bordeaux estates by reputation and price. Reds were ranked from first to fifth growths, nearly all in the Médoc, and the sweet whites of Sauternes and Barsac from superior first growth to second growth.
keyfacts: The 1855 classification gave Margaux 21 classed growths spanning every rank, including first growth Château Margaux.
The appellation covers four communes: Margaux-Cantenac, formed when Margaux and Cantenac merged, plus Arsac, Labarde and Soussans.
Vines grow on gravel terraces laid down by the Garonne, and a dense network of streams drains them.
Cabernet Sauvignon covers nearly 60% of the vineyard, Merlot rarely exceeds 30% of blends, and the wines are known for finesse and fruity aromas.

notes: Blackcurrant is the main fruit flavor in Margaux.
Aromas of violets are a hallmark of the appellation.
Wines from the southern communes, such as Cantenac and Labarde, tend to be more powerful, less fragrant and closer to plum.

blurb.text: A Bordeaux appellation within Haut-Médoc, for red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and others. It has 21 cru classé châteaux, more than any other commune in Bordeaux.
